candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 per-tile metadata
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 metadata follows the GEMINI metadata standard and is supplied per tile.
Metadata records the 5 km tile reference, projected and vertical reference systems, version number and reason for change.
Lineage distinguishes new imagery, partial revision and imagery examined with no change.
semantic_limits: Per-tile metadata supports lineage and freshness; it does not improve the vertical accuracy of a terrain sample.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 source TIN model
verified_facts: OS Terrain source DTM is captured as a triangulated irregular network using mass points and breaklines and/or automated photogrammetric techniques.
Grid and contour products are interpolated from the same source TIN.
The source model is subject to positional-accuracy and terrain-smoothness requirements.
semantic_limits: TIN fidelity is lineage evidence; OS Terrain 5 remains a secondary sanity source for this slot.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 data structure
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 grid heights are calculated at the centre of the pixel.
Mean high and low water heights are averaged per tile and may create a small discrete step between adjacent coastal tiles.
Spot heights are selected from an interpolated surface and are not guaranteed to be summits.
semantic_limits: Coastal tile-step and spot-height semantics require caution and do not replace the EA 1 m parcel measurement.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 product supply
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 is supplied nationally as 5 km by 5 km tiles.
The product is supplied quarterly in January, April, July and October as a full tile resupply.
Tile metadata is provided with the supply.
semantic_limits: Quarterly resupply is a freshness contract, not evidence that a particular tile changed.

candidates.name: Future of British mapping coordinate systems
verified_facts: OS states OSGB36 and ODN will remain the basis of OS mapping for the foreseeable future.
GNSS access to OSGB36 and ODN uses transformations from ETRS89 provided by OSTN15 and OSGM15.
OSGB36 and vertical mapping datums are accessed through separate horizontal and vertical transformations.
semantic_limits: Coordinate-system continuity does not reduce LiDAR terrain-source uncertainty.

candidates.name: Datum, ellipsoid and projection information
verified_facts: OS lists EPSG:27700 for OSGB36 British National Grid, EPSG:7405 for OSGB36 National Grid plus ODN height and EPSG:5701 for ODN.
OS lists EPSG transformation 7953 for the native OSTN15 transformation and 7711 for OSGM15 to ODN.
OS distinguishes WGS84, ETRS89, OSGB36 and vertical datum codes.
semantic_limits: CRS authority codes are reference controls; they are not parcel-elevation observations.

candidates.name: DSP dataset metadata guidance
verified_facts: DSP metadata includes use limitations, update frequency, lineage, coordinate reference system, geographic extent and revision dates.
Metadata is intended to explain how a dataset should be used and known limitations.
Data services and supporting information are exposed through dataset metadata.
semantic_limits: Metadata describes evidence and constraints; it cannot substitute for the underlying raster values.

candidates.name: LiDAR WMS preview guidance
verified_facts: EA provides WMS preview images for LiDAR Composite datasets.
Coverage metadata preview shows extents of published raster data.
EA states the preview is only an image and cannot be queried.
semantic_limits: WMS preview is visual QA only and is forbidden as a numeric elevation source.

candidates.name: Downloading Survey Data formats
verified_facts: EA LiDAR raster data is available in GeoTIFF format.
National LiDAR Programme and Composite raster data are supplied in 5 km tiles.
Point-cloud data is supplied as LAZ, the compressed form of LAS.
semantic_limits: Delivery format and tile size do not imply vertical precision.

candidates.name: LiDAR metadata and coverage maps
verified_facts: EA provides metadata and coverage maps through its LiDAR Capture Programme.
EA states that if no data is listed for a location, that location has not been surveyed by the programme.
EA LiDAR holdings described by this service are for England.
semantic_limits: Absence of coverage must fail closed; it must not be interpreted as zero elevation or zero height difference.

candidates.name: Current LiDAR capture programme
verified_facts: EA's capture programme exposes both the forward look for the current winter capture season and previous captured seasons.
The capture programme is the official place to inspect survey activity by season.
semantic_limits: Planned or captured survey activity is not equivalent to publication in the composite used by this slot.

candidates.name: GeoPackage spatial metadata index transition
verified_facts: LiDAR Composite downloads include a spatial metadata index in GeoPackage format.
The index describes spatial location and temporal extent of raster elevation data.
The GeoPackage replaces earlier Shapefile-based index delivery.
semantic_limits: Index geometry and temporal metadata are lineage evidence, not elevation measurements.

candidates.name: LiDAR Composite GeoTIFF transition
verified_facts: EA changed Composite delivery from ASCII to GeoTIFF.
GeoTIFF Composite files are supplied in 5 km tiles with elevations in metres.
The format change enabled more efficient storage and web services including WCS.
semantic_limits: The file-format transition does not by itself increase terrain accuracy.

candidates.name: National LIDAR Programme
verified_facts: The National LIDAR Programme provides 1 m elevation data for all England.
Phase 1 divided England into 302 survey blocks captured between January 2017 and February 2023.
Repeat surveys use incrementing phase numbers and publication continues quarterly.
semantic_limits: Programme coverage and phase lineage do not guarantee that every current Composite cell comes from the same survey date.

candidates.name: LiDAR point-density FAQ
verified_facts: A 1 m DSM survey has average point density of at least 1 point per square metre, 50 cm has 4 ppsqm and 25 cm has 16 ppsqm.
DTM point density under vegetation can be lower than the DSM density.
EA states point clouds are not regular grids, so density is not resolution.
semantic_limits: Point density cannot be substituted for raster cell size or vertical RMSE.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 downloads and schemas
verified_facts: OS publishes official XML schema resources for Terrain contour and gridded products.
Viewing Style Metadata resources are also provided.
These resources support validating the supplied product structures.
semantic_limits: Schema validity confirms structure, not the truth of a specific elevation value.
